newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 28.

text.p: DAILY TELEGRAPH

CREST URGES USERS TO BLOW WHISTLE ON SLUGGISH FIRMS Plans are being drawn up by directors of Crest to impose heavy fines on firms which cause delays to the electronic share settlement system. They are also asking users to blow the whistle on companies which have not mastered it.

Investigations have found thousands of matched, but unsettled transactions in the system, some of them several weeks old. Crest were planning to delete these transactions from the system over the weekend but acceded to City requests to keep them on, unsettled.
ROLLS-ROYCE IN TALKS TO SELL STEAM SIDE

Rolls Royce is talking with six companies over the possible sale of Parsons steam turbines and International Combustion boilermaker operations. There is suggestion that Siemens, the German industrial giant, is among the list of potential bidders. Although a deal is some way off, it is believed that the sale of Parsons is more advanced than discussions concerning international Combustion.
UNIT TRUSTS PUBLISH CODE OF CONDUCT

A voluntary code of conduct will be published today by the Association of Unit Trust & Investment Funds, in the hope of getting it adopted by its 140 members and bypassing the need for new regulations resulting from the recent discovery that Morgan Grenfell trusts had invested extensively in pre-listed securities.
THE TIMES
M&S TO INVADE OVER-THE-COUNTER PHARMACEUTICALS MARKET

Marks & Spencer is to introduce a range of over-the- counter pharmaceuticals in the new year. The range, that will bear the St Michael name, will include everything from paracetamol to vitamins and holistic health products, but will not include prescription drugs.
FRENCH COURT THREAT TO EUROTUNNEL JOB CUTS

The Channel Tunnel operator, Eurotunnel, has suffered a setback to its cost-cutting programme as trade unions in France and the UK reject the proposals to cut 657 jobs. Five French unions are to call in external accountants to review Eurotunnel's books and propose an alternative programme of cost-cutting measures. This move could lead to a court challenge in France.
CBI IN FIRING LINE OVER INVESTOR RIGHTS

The Confederation of British Industry will call for the debate over non-voting shares to be reopened this morning. The move will put the CBI on a crash course with Britain's largest institutional investors. The CBI says in its report on the future of listed smaller companies, that the greater use of two-tier share structures is essential to persuade private companies that they can float without losing control of their business.
GUARDIAN
800 MILLION POUND FAMILY STAKE DISCLOSED BY ROTHSCHILD

Sir Evelyn de Rothschild, the senior member of the Rothschild dynasty announced that the family has accumulated 800 million pounds stg of capital in the bank's Swiss holding company, Rothschild Continuation. The announcement is thought to be a move to stop the speculation that NM Rothschild's days as an independent bank are coming to an end.
N.IRELAND BOTTOM OF OFFICE LEAGUE

An earnings survey published today reveals that office workers in Northern Ireland are the worst paid in the UK, being paid between 10 and 40 per cent below the national average. The survey by Select Appointments a staffing agency, also shows that companies in Northern Ireland also provide significantly fewer benefits for staff despite the savings made on salaries.
ITALY FACES PROTRACTED BATTLE OVER NEXT ROUND OF STATE
SELL-OFFS

Inter-party feuding in Italy is threatening the next round of sell-offs despite the success of the sale of shares in the state-controlled energy group Ente Nazionale Idrocarburi . Treasury minister, Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told reporters at the weekend that the government was determined to meet it's goal of selling the state's 64 per cent stake in telecoms holding Stet by March 1997. He also promised to launch the privatisation of electricity utility Enel, and Autostrade the motorway toll operator. One of the main forces against the privatisation is the government-supporting Communist Refoundation which is ideologically opposed to the sell-off.
INDEPENDENT
CLARKE'S ADVISERS SEEK RATE INCREASE

In a report due to be published on Friday, five of Kenneth Clarke's six advisers will call for higher interest rates and no tax cuts. The pre-Budget report by the Treasury's Panel of Independent Forecasters will argue that the Chancellor should not use the Budget next month to boost growth in the months ahead of the election, with only one of the six advisers believing that the economy could grow faster without triggering higher inflation.
4,000 "ROGUE DIRECTORS' ON LOOSE IN UK COMPANIES

According to a report to be published today, more than 4,000 directors are working in UK companies who have at least 10 failed companies behind them. The report by the CCN Group, an information services company, blasts Britain's inadequate laws for dealing with the 'rogue directors'.
MURDOCH'S $1 BILLION SHARE ISSUE TO BE DELAYED FOR A WEEK

The controversial share issue by Rupert Murdoch's News America Holdings is to be postponed by at least a week according to sources close to the company's bankers. This confirms reports that the $1 billion dollar US issue which will be convertible into shares of BSkyB, Mr Murdoch's 40 per cent owned satellite broadcaster, would not be priced until after the quarterly profits of BSkyB are announced at the company's annual meeting on Friday.
